passages.note: Bill details page: SB 101 digest and enactment history for the instrument Soliday later voted on.

passages.provision_quote: A governmental entity may substantially burden a person's exercise of religion only if the governmental entity demonstrates that application of the burden to the person: (1) is in furtherance of a compelling governmental interest; and (2) is the least restrictive means of furthering that compelling governmental interest.
passages.note: Enrolled bill text giving the operative compelling-interest/least-restrictive-means exemption test Soliday voted to enact.
House roll call 305: Soliday voted Yea on final passage of SB 101.

rows.reasoning: Soliday voted Yea on final passage of SB 101 (2015), a single-subject Religious Freedom Restoration Act whose operative text lets a person assert a claim or defense against a governmental burden on their religion unless the government shows a compelling interest pursued by the least restrictive means. That exemption mechanism, available to any person (not only religious organizations) and subject to a government override (not "complete autonomy"), matches the rung text "protect religious freedom and allow faith-based exemptions from laws that conflict with sincere religious beliefs."
